mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in FEDFUNDS above 2% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 of more than 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in UNRATE above 6% for three consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which raises wage pressures and input costs, ultimately compressing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals weakening industrial production, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month MA for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in UNRATE above 6% and a fall in PAYEMS below its 12-month moving average signals labor market imbalances, which increase cost pressures and reduce hiring, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent increase in HOUST and a decline in GDPC1 over two months signals housing-driven demand deceleration, which disproportionately affects consumer spending and drags equity valuations lower, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-month MA AND GDPC1 < 12-month MA for two months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in CPIAUCSL below 1% for three consecutive months signals deflationary risk, which increases real discount rates and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in RSAFS above its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months signals rising household savings and reduced consumption, which lowers corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-month MA for five consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 35% of triggered episodes.
